docs.title: YeetnGreet docs
docs.text:
YeetnGreet helps IT admins onboard and offboard Microsoft 365 users from a Windows PC — without putting tenant data in our cloud.

Microsoft Graph runs on your technicians’ machines. We only use the cloud for your YeetnGreet license and billing. YeetnGreet is proprietary software.

docs.title: Support
docs.text: Need help with YeetnGreet? Start with the docs, then email us. This page is for IT admins running the Windows app against Microsoft 365 tenants.

docs.title: How to get help
docs.text:
Email support@yeetngreet.app.

That is the public support address. Please do not open GitHub Issues for product support — the application repository is private, and Issues are not a customer support channel. YeetnGreet is proprietary software.

docs.title: Check the docs first
docs.text:
Many how-tos are already covered here:

Topic Docs Install and launch Install First tenant sign-in and preview First run Offboard / onboard / schedules Jobs License and unused-license reports Reports Switching tenants Multi-tenant Plans and limits Pricing and licensing What we store Privacy

If the docs answer it, you save a round-trip — and we can spend support time on the harder cases.

docs.title: What to include in your email
docs.text:
The more context you send up front, the faster we can help. Please include:

  1. App version — Help → About in YeetnGreet (or the version shown on the About screen)
  2. Windows version — for example Windows 11 23H2, or winver output
  3. Plan — Free, Starter, Growth, Business, Scale, Large, or Enterprise
  4. Tenant domain — the Microsoft 365 domain you were working in (for example contoso.com), not passwords or secrets
  5. Steps to reproduce — what you clicked or ran, what you expected, and what happened
  6. Screenshots — if the issue is in the UI (redact PII where you can)

Do not send secrets

Do not include passwords, refresh tokens, client secrets, or full mailbox contents. Tenant domain and a short error message are enough for most Graph failures.

docs.title: Response expectations
docs.text:
We monitor support@yeetngreet.app and reply on business days. Timing varies with volume and how much detail is in the initial email — we do not publish a formal SLA here.

Urgent production blockers still go to the same address; put a clear subject line (for example Offboard blocked — Graph 403) so we can prioritize.

docs.text:
1. Launch YeetnGreet on the technician PC

  4. Open Offboard or Onboard and use Preview (or equivalent review step) before confirm

Confirm the tenant

docs.title: Install
docs.text: YeetnGreet is a Windows single-file app (YeetnGreet.exe) that uses Microsoft Edge WebView2 for the UI. Install once on each technician PC that will run jobs.

docs.title: 1. Get the app
docs.text:
Public Windows downloads are not available yet. YeetnGreet ships as a single-file YeetnGreet.exe with the release. Until then:

  1. Join the waitlist on the pricing page
  2. When your build is ready, save YeetnGreet.exe somewhere durable (for example C:\Tools\YeetnGreet\ or a shared tech folder)

Coming with the release

Download links will appear here when the public release ships. Waitlist members get access through the preregister path first.

docs.title: 2. WebView2
docs.text:
Most Windows 10/11 machines already have the Evergreen WebView2 Runtime. If the app cannot start the UI:

  1. Install (or repair) the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime
  2. Run YeetnGreet again

docs.title: 3. First launch
docs.text:
1. Double-click YeetnGreet.exe (no separate installer required)
  2. Allow Windows SmartScreen / firewall prompts if your environment shows them
  3. You should see the YeetnGreet shell ready for tenant sign-in

Placeholder UI — replace with a real capture from %LOCALAPPDATA%\YeetnGreet or the running app on a technician laptop.

docs.title: 4. Tenant sign-in
docs.text:
Sign in with an account that can administer the customer Microsoft 365 tenant you are working in. Graph calls leave from this PC to Microsoft — not through YeetnGreet’s vendor cloud.

Admin consent first

Each customer tenant needs an admin to grant consent for YeetnGreet's Microsoft Graph and Exchange Online permissions before the first job. See Admin permissions and consent for the full list.

Placeholder — Microsoft sign-in happens on the technician PC.

What our cloud sees

License and billing metadata for your YeetnGreet account only. Not customer mail, files, or directory content used during jobs.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Continue with First run to complete a safe preview job.

docs.title: Admin permissions and consent
docs.text:
YeetnGreet changes users, mailboxes, licenses, and devices in your Microsoft 365 tenant. Microsoft requires an administrator in each tenant you manage to approve (grant admin consent for) the permissions below before YeetnGreet can run jobs there.

Use this page as the checklist for your Global Administrator, or for your own change ticket.

Admin consent is per tenant

Consent granted in one tenant does not carry over to another. If you manage more than one tenant, repeat it for every tenant you add to YeetnGreet. Granting admin consent for Microsoft Graph application permissions needs a Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator in that tenant.

docs.title: How YeetnGreet signs in
docs.text:
Sign-in mode What runs the job What your admin approves App-only (recommended for unattended and scheduled jobs) The YeetnGreet app, with a certificate, with no admin account signed in The application permissions and directory roles below Interactive An admin signs in to the tenant in the browser The delegated permissions below, plus admin roles on the admin's account

Either way, tokens are requested for the tenant you selected. YeetnGreet refuses to run a job if Microsoft returns a token for a different tenant.

docs.title: App-only: application permissions
docs.text: Grant these in your tenant for the YeetnGreet app (Enterprise applications → YeetnGreet → Permissions → Grant admin consent). All are Application permissions.

docs.title: Microsoft Graph
docs.text:
Permission Why YeetnGreet needs it User.ReadWrite.All Create onboard accounts and update user details: manager, usage location, address-list visibility, and moving direct reports to a new manager. User.EnableDisableAccount.All Block sign-in for leavers and enable new hires' accounts. User-PasswordProfile.ReadWrite.All Reset the leaver's password and set the new hire's first password. User.RevokeSessions.All Sign the leaver out of every active session. UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite.All Remove the leaver's MFA methods: Authenticator, phone, FIDO2, Windows Hello, software OATH, and email. LicenseAssignment.ReadWrite.All Assign licenses at onboard, remove them at offboard, and read license SKUs for the license audit. GroupMember.ReadWrite.All Add new hires to groups and remove leavers from groups. RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory Remove Entra admin role assignments from leavers. Directory.ReadWrite.All Read tenant details, memberships, and direct reports, and update directory links the narrower permissions above don't cover. MailboxSettings.ReadWrite Set the leaver's out-of-office auto-reply. Files.ReadWrite.All Share the leaver's OneDrive with their manager or the handoff person. DeviceManagementManagedDevices.ReadWrite.All Find the leaver's Intune-managed devices. DeviceManagementManagedDevices.PrivilegedOperations.All Retire those Intune devices. Requires admin consent. Without consent, the app greys out Retire. Only needed if you use Retire Intune devices. Reports.Read.All Read Microsoft 365 mail activity for the Unused licenses and License audit reports.

YeetnGreet does not request application Mail.Send. Report email delivery is interactive-only (see below).

docs.title: Office 365 Exchange Online
docs.text: Permission Why YeetnGreet needs it Exchange.ManageAsApp Connect to Exchange Online without a user, so YeetnGreet can convert the leaver's mailbox to shared, grant Full Access to the handoff person, and hide the mailbox from the address list.

docs.title: Directory roles for the YeetnGreet app
docs.text:
Microsoft requires an admin role on the app as well as the permissions above for some actions. In your tenant, assign these roles to the YeetnGreet enterprise application (Entra admin center → Roles & admins):

Role Why Exchange Administrator Exchange Online only accepts Exchange.ManageAsApp when the app also holds an Exchange admin role. Needed for the mailbox steps. User Administrator Microsoft requires at least this role for an app to reset passwords.

Offboarding an admin

Microsoft blocks lower-privileged roles from disabling, resetting, or removing MFA for other administrators. If you offboard someone who holds an admin role, the app may need Privileged Authentication Administrator. Otherwise, do those steps in the Entra admin center.

docs.title: Interactive: delegated permissions
docs.text:
When an admin signs in, YeetnGreet requests these delegated Microsoft Graph permissions. They match the app-only Graph names above, plus Directory.AccessAsUser.All (act as the signed-in admin) and Mail.Send (report email):

User.ReadWrite.All, User.EnableDisableAccount.All, User-PasswordProfile.ReadWrite.All, Directory.AccessAsUser.All, User.RevokeSessions.All, LicenseAssignment.ReadWrite.All, UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite.All, MailboxSettings.ReadWrite, GroupMember.ReadWrite.All, RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory, Directory.ReadWrite.All, Files.ReadWrite.All, DeviceManagementManagedDevices.ReadWrite.All, DeviceManagementManagedDevices.PrivilegedOperations.All, Reports.Read.All, Mail.Send

Interactive sign-in uses Microsoft's Microsoft Graph Command Line Tools app. The first time, approve the consent prompt and tick Consent on behalf of your organization, or grant admin consent to that app in your tenant.

Consent alone doesn't let an admin run the job. The signed-in account needs an active admin role too:

Role on the signed-in account Why User Administrator (or Global Administrator / Privileged Role Administrator) Required to disable accounts and reset passwords. YeetnGreet checks for it and stops before a Live job if it's missing. Exchange Administrator Needed for the Exchange Online sign-in that runs the mailbox steps.

Report email delivery

Sending a report by email uses delegated Mail.Send and works only in interactive sign-in. In app-only mode, email delivery is unavailable — use a webhook or save the report locally instead. Application Mail.Send is not used.

docs.title: What YeetnGreet does not need
docs.text:
• Access beyond your work account to use YeetnGreet itself: signing in to YeetnGreet for team and license features only uses User.Read against your own work account. It never grants access to your tenant's data.
  • On-premises Active Directory: YeetnGreet works with cloud-only Microsoft 365 (Entra ID). On-premises and hybrid Active Directory aren't supported yet.
  • Application Mail.Send: not requested. Email reports are interactive-only (delegated Mail.Send).

docs.title: Checklist for each tenant
docs.text:
1. Grant admin consent for every Microsoft Graph and Exchange Online permission above
  2. App-only: assign Exchange Administrator and User Administrator to the YeetnGreet enterprise app
  3. Interactive: confirm the signed-in admin account has User Administrator (or higher) and Exchange Administrator
  4. If you use Retire Intune devices: confirm admin consent for DeviceManagementManagedDevices.PrivilegedOperations.All (otherwise Retire stays greyed out)
  5. Run a Preview in First run before any Live job

docs.title: Schedules
docs.text: Schedule onboard, offboard, and report jobs to run later on the same technician PC where you created them.

docs.title: How scheduling works
docs.text:
1. Build the job as usual (users, template, delivery options)
  2. Choose a future run time instead of Run now
  3. Leave the PC able to run YeetnGreet at that time (powered on, user session / auth as your process requires)

Placeholder — schedule a job for later on this PC.

Schedules are local to the PC

A scheduled job does not run in YeetnGreet’s cloud. If the PC is off or YeetnGreet cannot run, the job will not execute until conditions allow — plan cutovers accordingly.

docs.title: Good uses
docs.text:
• Friday evening offboards after payroll clears
  • Monday morning onboard batches
  • Weekly license or unused licenses reports with delivery

docs.title: License audit
docs.text:
See which Microsoft 365 licenses are assigned — with SKU detail, mail activity (last 90 days), and attention rows for disabled + licensed and no mail users.

In the app this is the User licensing card on Reports after you run a license report.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Quarterly license hygiene
  • Before a renewal or true-up
  • After a merger / tenant consolidation wave
  • Finding named users to reclaim before you cut prepaid licenses

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select the tenant and sign in
  2. Open Reports → Run license report
  3. Review the User licensing summary and table (filter by name, UPN, or license)
  4. Pair with What-if for priced reclaim and scenario planning
  5. Export or deliver as needed

See Samples for anonymized SKU counts and named-user examples.

Plans

Free includes a limited license-report preview. Full named-user audit, exact savings, and exports are on paid plans. See Pricing and licensing.

Mail activity

No-mail detection needs Reports.Read.All. If mail metrics are missing, re-sign in to grant the permission — the app will not treat every licensed user as inactive when mail data did not load.

docs.title: Reports overview
docs.text: YeetnGreet reports help you see Microsoft 365 license waste from the same technician PC model as onboard/offboard jobs. You run Graph queries locally, then export or deliver results yourself.

docs.title: Report types
docs.text:
Report Purpose License audit Who is licensed, mail activity (90d), disabled+licensed and no-mail attention rows Unused licenses Unused prepaid licenses and licenses on disabled accounts What-if Reclaim savings plus named scenario planning (moves, hires, cuts) Samples Anonymized example output

In the app these appear together on Reports after you run a license report — not as separate menu items.

docs.title: How to run
docs.text:
1. Select the managed tenant and sign in
  2. Open Reports → Run license report
  3. Review User licensing (audit) and What-if (reclaim + scenario planner)
  4. Edit unit costs on the what-if card and Save costs for a saved tenant price
  5. Optionally build a named scenario, then export HTML/PDF, schedule a recurring run, or send via Delivery

Placeholder — license audit summary in the app.

Plans

Free includes a limited license-report preview (bucketed savings, no SKU/$ detail or named users). Full SKU tables, exact savings, named users, scenario export, and deliveries are on paid plans. See Pricing and licensing.

Data path

Report queries use Microsoft Graph from the technician PC (Reports.Read.All for mail activity). Exports and delivery stay under your control — YeetnGreet does not host a data lake of customer report content. What-if scenarios are projections only; they never change licenses in the tenant.

Savings / mo = (Unused + Disabled) × Unit. Inactive (no-mail) users are not priced here — inactive is not confirmed waste.

  2. Remove disabled-assigned on E3 (all 12) — drops enabled and consumed together
  3. Move 10 licenses E3 → Business Premium

docs.title: Unused licenses
docs.text:
Find prepaid licenses that are not assigned, and licenses still stuck on disabled accounts — before the renewal meeting.

In the app this is the Unused / Disabled columns on the license report’s What-if table (not a separate Reports submenu).

docs.title: Signals
docs.text: Signal Meaning Unused Prepaid enabled licenses minus consumed (available capacity you are still paying for) Disabled License assignments on accounts with sign-in blocked No mail (90d) Enabled licensed users with no send/receive/read in the mail activity window — shown under User licensing for review. Not priced as reclaim because inactive is not confirmed waste.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Monthly license hygiene
  • After offboard waves (catch stragglers still licensed while disabled)
  • When finance asks “where can we cut?”

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select the tenant and sign in
  2. Open Reports → Run license report
  3. On What-if, review Unused and Disabled per SKU
  4. Open User licensing for named disabled+licensed and no-mail users
  5. Validate in the Microsoft 365 admin center before you remove SKUs or reduce quantities
  6. Export or deliver if needed

Example screenshot — idle licenses with per-SKU savings. Marketing sample numbers are synthetic and checked so row math totals correctly.

Validate before reclaim

Unused and disabled signals are a starting point. Confirm with your process (shared mailboxes, break-glass accounts, seasonal staff) before you remove SKUs. Sample savings on the marketing site are examples only — not a guarantee.

docs.text: Pair this view with What-if: set unit costs, then read Savings / mo = (Unused + Disabled) × Unit per SKU. Use the scenario planner on the same card to model reclaim steps without changing the tenant.

docs.title: What-if
docs.text:
Plan license changes before you touch the admin center. What-if lives on the Reports page after you run a license report. It is read-only — nothing in the tenant changes.

The same card has two layers:

  1. Reclaim savings — price unused prepaid licenses and licenses on disabled accounts
  2. Scenario planner — name a plan, stack steps, see before/after counts and cost deltas

docs.title: Price sources
docs.text:
Unit costs power both reclaim and scenarios. Graph does not expose your invoice price. Each SKU shows where the number came from:

Label Meaning list-price estimate US direct-purchase list fallback until you save enter cost You edited the unit cost but have not saved yet saved tenant price Stored on this managed tenant after Save costs

Always validate against your Microsoft bill before committing to a cut or buy.

docs.title: Reclaim savings
docs.text:
Bucket Meaning How it is priced Unused prepaid licenses Enabled licenses you pay for that are not assigned (enabled − consumed) Unused count × unit cost / mo Disabled + licensed Licenses still assigned to blocked accounts Disabled-assigned count × unit cost / mo

Potential monthly savings = unused cost + disabled-assigned cost, summed across SKUs.

docs.title: What is not priced in reclaim
docs.text: Inactive licensed users (enabled, but no mail send/receive/read in the last 90 days) appear under User licensing so you can review them. They are not added into reclaim dollars because inactive is not confirmed waste — someone may still need that license.

docs.title: Scenario planner
docs.text:
Start from the tenant’s current licenses (from the latest full report) and build a named scenario:

Step What it models Remove unused licenses Drop prepaid capacity that is not assigned (blank quantity = all unused on that SKU) Remove disabled-assigned licenses Reduce enabled, consumed, and disabled-assigned together for licenses still sitting on blocked accounts (blank quantity = all disabled-assigned on that SKU) Move licenses (SKU → SKU) Move N assigned licenses from one SKU to another (for example E3 → Business Premium). To can be a SKU the tenant does not own yet, picked from the built-in price list Add licenses (planned hires) Increase enabled + consumed for upcoming headcount Remove licenses (planned cuts) Reduce enabled (and consumed) for planned reductions

Every subscribed SKU gets a unit cost (list-price estimate by default) with an editable cost field — including fully used SKUs. If a step asks for more licenses than exist, the app applies what is available and shows the amount applied. Totals warn when any SKU still has no price.

For each scenario the app shows:

  • Before / after prepaid enabled license counts per SKU
  • Unit cost with its price source label
  • Monthly and annual cost difference (after − before)

Scenarios are saved per managed tenant, can be reopened later, and export or deliver like other reports (HTML, CSV, optional PDF). Delivery uses the tenant’s existing channels.

Keep scenarios named

Use clear names (“Q4 reclaim + E3→Business Premium”) so the next tech on the account can reuse them.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Renewal or true-up prep — reclaim unused and disabled licenses
  • Quote a right-size move (E3 → Business Premium) before you buy
  • Model planned hires or cuts without changing Graph
  • Pair with unused licenses and the license audit

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select the managed tenant and sign in.
  2. Open Reports → Run license report.
  3. On What-if savings:
  4. Review reclaim Unused, Disabled, Unit / mo, and Savings / mo for every SKU
  5. Edit unit costs if needed; click Save costs to store only the prices you entered as a saved tenant price
  6. In Scenario planner:
  7. Name the scenario and add steps
  8. Review before/after counts and monthly/annual deltas (and any quantity or missing-price warnings)
  9. Save to store on this tenant, or Open a saved scenario
  10. Optionally Export / Export PDF, or deliver via the tenant’s report channels

Community / Free preview shows a savings bucket without SKU-level dollars, named users, or scenario export — upgrade for full detail.

docs.title: Hybrid AD
docs.text: Optional hybrid Active Directory support can be enabled per tenant when an organization needs on-prem identity alongside Entra ID.

docs.title: What it is for
docs.text:
• Tenants still running hybrid join / synced identities
  • Offboard and onboard paths that must respect on-prem + cloud steps your team defines

docs.title: How to think about it
docs.text:
Topic Guidance Scope Optional per managed tenant — enable only where needed Where it runs Still on the technician PC model; not “upload AD to YeetnGreet cloud” Availability Hybrid support is planned; pricing follows the same licensed-user bands on the pricing page

Cloud-only tenants

If a tenant is cloud-only Entra, you can ignore hybrid settings entirely.

docs.title: Multi-tenant
docs.text: Switch between the Microsoft 365 tenants on your account without mixing up context — as long as you confirm the active tenant before Live work. Licensed users are pooled across all tenants on the account for billing.

docs.title: Switching tenants
docs.text:
1. Open the tenant switcher in YeetnGreet
  2. Select the tenant you are about to work on
  3. Confirm domain / display name matches the ticket
  4. Continue with onboard, offboard, or reports

Placeholder — multi-tenant switcher.

Wrong-tenant rule

Preview and type-to-confirm protect actions, but they do not fix picking the wrong organization. Habit: read the tenant name before every confirm.
